records.assessment: Stable-inode feature bit 0x0800 and ext4_has_feature_stable_inodes remain in the native header. The cryptops moved to fs/ext4/crypto.c and use has_stable_inodes plus has_32bit_inodes=1; fscrypt policy validation checks stable numbers, 32-bit inode numbers and maximum data-unit index. Keep these native evolved interfaces instead of restoring the old get_ino_and_lblk_bits callback. This preserves policy eligibility and IV uniqueness constraints.

Both unique merge hunks examined. Native ext4_should_use_dio and ext4_dio_alignment retain encryption alignment/eligibility checks and shared/exclusive unlock selection before buffered-write fallback. Native readpage bio setup retains both fscrypt_set_bio_crypt_ctx and ext4_set_bio_post_read_ctx, with the mempool-backed post-read context and native error completion. Historical helper names and bio allocation ordering need not be restored; no inline crypto or verity step is lost.

All five files reviewed. Native superblock owns encoding/flags and unloads encoding on teardown and mount failure. generic_set_sb_d_ops selects generic casefold operations with fscrypt revalidation; native name setup/hash use sb encoding and generic_ci_validate_strict_name. generic_ci_d_compare keeps the safe shortname snapshot for concurrent rename and generic_ci_match handles decrypt/compare/free. These native implementations preserve generic casefold functionality with later fixes; do not reintroduce per-ext4 callbacks or old strict-mode macros.

Native ext4_fname_setup_ci_filename computes SipHash once, returns allocation/hash errors, and retains the full ext4_filename result. dx_probe/index creation and insertion use the precomputed hashes. ext4_match checks hash/minor-hash only when casefold state was initialized and compatibility fallback permits it, then performs generic_ci_match. Keep the later key-add race and casefold compatibility guards, rather than reverting to the historical unconditional encrypted hash fast path.

All unique remerge hunks examined: inline deletion adopts the no-handle generic helper, directory search/delete receive buffer bounds, and unlink error paths coexist with the old lblk argument. The merge incorrectly used bh->b_size for inline search; 7dda6587abc7 fixes this to buf_size. Native search retains that correction plus the newer hash-tail bounds check; native inline/delete/unlink paths use the evolved no-lblk interfaces, correct error return and fast-commit replay logic. Do not replay the merge-introduced bounds regression.

The single-hunk mis-merge fix is present in native ext4_search_dir: ext4_check_dir_entry receives search_buf and buf_size, not bh->b_size. The obsolete lblk parameter was removed by the upstream-aligned directory implementation. Newer native directory-hash-tail bounds validation is also retained; applying the old patch literally would only conflict with these corrected interfaces.

All unique resolutions examined across dir.c/ext4.h/namei.c. The removed private d_compare/d_hash callbacks are replaced by native generic operations; generic_ci_d_compare preserves stable shortname handling during rename. Native __ext4_unlink keeps fast-commit skip_remove_dentry, normal error paths and journal/reference cleanup. The old lblk plumbing was superseded by name-based fake-dirent validation in the upstream-aligned series; do not reintroduce it or duplicate private casefold callbacks.

All unique resolutions examined. Generic dentry operations now include casefold and fscrypt revalidation and are selected by generic_set_sb_d_ops, replacing both the suppressed ext4 table and old mount-time assignment. The old decrypt/compare/free logic is native generic_ci_match, which frees decrypted storage on failures and after comparison, and enforces strict encoding. Preserve that native helper and its caller error handling instead of reintroducing ext4_ci_compare.

Native ext4fs_dirhash, ext4_fname_setup_ci_filename and ext4_match retain the encryption-key guards from this fix. No-key name matching uses fscrypt_match_name. Native matching additionally prevents use of uninitialized precomputed hashes if a key appeared after name preparation. Keep both missing-key behavior and the subsequent key-add race fix; code already represented upstream.

The unique header resolution changed the historical __ext4_unlink handle argument and omitted the obsolete ext4_ci_compare declaration. Current LTS header/implementation agree on the later no-handle unlink API, where lookup/key setup occur before the internally started transaction to avoid unsafe allocation context. The private comparison helper is superseded by generic_ci_match. Keep current call/definition coherence and native transaction lifetime, not the old intermediate declaration.

Native ext4_should_use_dio delegates to ext4_dio_alignment, which rejects verity/journal-data/inline-data and requires fscrypt_dio_supported for encrypted files with filesystem-block alignment. Both read and write paths use the predicate. Native ext4_iomap_begin calls fscrypt_limit_io_blocks before ext4_set_iomap to preserve DUN contiguity; the native limit helper handles IV_INO_LBLK_32 wrap. Keep evolved interfaces and subsequent atomic-write coverage checks. No direct-I/O encryption capability from the original patch is omitted.

The original fix supplied a fifth NULL argument to the then-ACK-only ext4_find_entry signature during rename rollback. The old lblk argument was removed by 7491ab39cbb2; current native ext4_resetent uses the correct four-argument signature and retrieves old.inlined, handles errors and releases the reacquired buffer. Preserve the actual rollback operation and newer inline state tracking, not the superseded signature shim.

Complete seven-file upstream-sync patch reviewed: native dir.c uses fake-dirent names/checksum types and validates record bounds; all declarations/callers omit obsolete lblk arguments; ialloc uses HALF_MD4 group placement; sysfs advertises encrypted_casefold. Native inline read and search bounds include later LTS fixes, and encrypted-inode creation forbids inline data before context installation. Keep those fixes and the upstream-aligned casefold representation. The only separate namei change is the already-applied casefold rmdir transaction-deadlock fix 22157454367a.

The unique merge resolution preserves fscrypt_limit_io_blocks while adding flags to ext4_set_iomap. Both are already in native ext4_iomap_begin. It additionally checks atomic-write mapping coverage after DUN limiting and before returning the mapping. Keep this native sequence; replaying the older merge result would discard newer I/O constraints.
